Автор: Adrian Pape

Hey, it's Adrian! Last week I wrote that a correction looked more likely than a breakout. Bitcoin clearly doesn’t read my newsletter. From $76k last Thursday it ran to about $87k by Tuesday, in the same week the 10-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since 2007. That’s a real sign of strength. The buyers are back too. The spot ETFs took in about $2.3 billion in four sessions, after losing over $1 billion the week before. Today Bitcoin sits at $83.6k after a flush of long liquidations, right at the price block that held it down for most of the year. I’ve moved to a fully risk-on stance and added leverage to my long term position, because I think we have entered the early bull phase of the cycle. Let’s get into the broader picture and how to set up for the coming week: ️ ⚡ On today's Episode: 📈 Market Update – The 10-year yield hit 5.1%, a 19-year high, Brent is back above $105, the Fed hiked and October hike odds jumped to 71%. Bitcoin still ran from $76k to $87k. 🔊 Market Pulse – The June low never broke the Realized Price, the new buyers’ cost basis crossed above the long-term holders’, and ETFs took in about $2.3 billion in four sessions. The next test sits at $95k–$97k. 🐂 Project and Alpha Insights – UNI, HYPE, NEAR and ZEC: what’s working, what’s still missing, and how I’d enter. I added leverage to my Bitcoin position with a liquidation price at $38k, plus a short-term long at $82.3k. The macro state of the market. Market Overview Over the last six months, almost everything that usually hurts Bitcoin has happened: The 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.1% on Wednesday, the first time in 19 years. It started 2026 at 4.15%. Brent oil is back above $105, and the war in Iran remains unresolved. The Fed hiked last week, and the odds of another hike in October jumped to 75% this week. The CLARITY Act failed in the Senate. AI dystopian panic fantasies is all over the news. Polymarket has the Democrats taking the House at 93% and the Senate at 66% in the November midterms. I’ve written about most of these risks here over the last months. They still didn’t stop me from moving into a fully risk-on stance. Why? Because Bitcoin moves in adoption and market cycles. Who holds it, how the market is structured and how much credit and leverage sits in the system can matter more than the macro. And the macro isn’t only working against Bitcoin.
